messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Help with difference in dregrees of freedom between Lavaan and Mplus
parts:
I can't speak for Mplus, but lavaan's default setting with categorical data is conditional.x=TRUE. That means the exogenous predictors are partialed out of all endogenous variables, and the model is fitted to the residual covariance matrix among endogenous variables.  The baseline model is fitted using the same rules (compare summary(base_cx) and summary(base_fx) in the example below), so endogenous variables are allowed to covary via sharing common predictors (but they are conditionally independent: residual covariances == 0), whereas they are marginally independent in the model where exogenous variables are merely fixed (fixed.x=TRUE) but not partialed out (conditional.x=FALSE).

That is why your degrees of freedom seem to be smaller in lavaan's default baseline model, which might be misinterpreted as signifying the baseline model is less (rather than more) restrictive than your hypothesized model.  The degrees of freedom are larger (as expected) in Mplus output, so it appears they are doing something like fixed.x=TRUE and conditional.x=FALSE.  You can use those arguments with your data to see if they result in the same baseline-model output in Mplus and lavaan.


HS9 <- HolzingerSwineford1939[,c("x1","x2","x3","x4")]
HSbinary <- cbind(HolzingerSwineford1939[ , c("agemo","ageyr","sex")],
                  as.data.frame( lapply(HS9, cut, 2, labels=FALSE) ))
HS.model <- ' f  =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4
              f ~ b1*ageyr + b2*agemo + sex
        b1 == b2*12 # so b1 and b2 both represent same linear effect of age
'
fit_cx <- cfa(HS.model, data=HSbinary, ordered=paste0("x", 1:4))
fit_fx <- cfa(HS.model, data=HSbinary, ordered=paste0("x", 1:4),
              conditional.x = FALSE) # override the default setting
## fit baseline models so we can see more information about them
base_cx <- update(fit_cx, model = lav_partable_independence(fit_cx))
base_fx <- update(fit_fx, model = lav_partable_independence(fit_fx))


## compare estimated baseline models to summary() output
fitNames <- c("chisq","df","pvalue")

print(fitMeasures(fit_fx, output = "text",
            fit.measures = c(fitNames,
                             paste(fitNames, "scaled", sep = "."),
                             "chisq.scaling.factor",
                             paste("baseline", fitNames, sep = "."),
                             paste("baseline", fitNames, "scaled", sep = "."),
                             "baseline.chisq.scaling.factor")),
      add.h0 = TRUE)
base_fx # verify we fit the same model

print(fitMeasures(fit_cx, output = "text",
                  fit.measures = c(fitNames,
                                   paste(fitNames, "scaled", sep = "."),
                                   "chisq.scaling.factor",
                                   paste("baseline", fitNames, sep = "."),
                                   paste("baseline", fitNames, "scaled", sep = "."),
                                   "baseline.chisq.scaling.factor")),
      add.h0 = TRUE)
base_cx # verify we fit the same model

## now you can compare results from different baseline models
